key_insight: GALÆXI is an architecture-agnostic, GPU-accelerated high-order DGSEM framework that enables scalable compressible-flow simulations across NVIDIA and AMD hardware.
engineering_relevance: It helps CFD teams run production-scale turbulent-flow simulations efficiently on heterogeneous supercomputers without rewriting algorithms for each GPU vendor.
method: Implemented a high-order discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) on unstructured hexahedral grids.
Bridged Fortran code to vendor-specific GPU backends using CUDA C++ for NVIDIA and HIP C++ for AMD.
Verified accuracy with manufactured solutions and validated flow physics on compressible Taylor-Green-vortex and airfoil LES cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous convergence verification, agreement with reference Taylor-Green-vortex solutions, near-ideal strong/weak scaling, and a 67.1B-DOF run on 65,536 AMD MI250X devices at 82.6% parallel efficiency.
watch_item: Performance and portability depend on maintaining two backend implementations, which can increase software complexity and tuning effort across GPU vendors.
paper_title: An Architecture-Agnostic High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Framework for Compressible Flows
